what: Frozen-plan construction test of the eaglepass1917 key, run 23 Nov 2026 about 10:30 EST by an AI agent (Claude Opus 5.5). The plan (SHA-256 f6372af4f261a71559eb772e0a757856081aa68812c3977ff34f8ba493cedee2) and the search script are kept outside this package because they also hold keys printed in the Narvaez book.
honest_start: The TIRANO fold was first noticed by eye in the eleven recovered pairs; the search below checks it and looks for any other fit. It is not a blind discovery.
constructions: keyword alphabet (keyword without repeats, rest of the alphabet ascending or descending), 26 and 27 letters (27 with N-tilde), (a) folded on itself about every axis, (b) written in two rows and paired with every offset, second row as written or reversed; empty keyword = plain alphabet (shifted and reversed pairings)
keyword_lists: W1 corpus words of 3-15 letters (Archivo Santander XIV OCR + Spanish readings of 13 Mexican targets in this repository); W2 the 100 words of the consular key list, Narvaez p. 338 fig. 9, as read blind; W3 words of 3-15 letters in our OCR of Narvaez ch. IX; W4 MURCIELAGO, ANTONIO, ESCULTOR, RODIN, TREINTAIUNO, TREINTAYUNO
hit_rule: a candidate must give exactly the 21 observed cipher->plain values

control_positive.how: fold keys from 50 random corpus words (seed 7), restricted to the same 21 letters

control_random_how: random reciprocal keys (seed 11): 2,000 on 26 letters with two fixed letters, 1,000 on 27 letters with one
family_note: The same search finds that the 1915 'Clave Garduno' table printed by Narvaez (p. 311) is the fold of the 27-letter keyword alphabet GARDUNO (with N-tilde); no fit for row 2 of Seguin's 1916 plana (fig. 7). The tables themselves are not reproduced here.
